players.product: Advantage2 annealing quantum computers and dual-rail superconducting gate-model systems (Quantum Circuits)

quarterly_data.signal: D-Wave 10-K: remaining performance obligations were $13.4 million at December 31, 2025, of which approximately 14% is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months, 33% within two years and 52% within three years; deferred revenue fell to $3,338 thousand from $19,356 thousand as the 2025 system sale was recognized. Cloud revenue grew at a 24 percent compound annual rate between 2018, when the Leap service was introduced, and the end of 2025; the Leap service is available in 42 countries, with physical systems in Burnaby (British Columbia), at the University of Southern California's Information Sciences Institute and at Davidson Technologies in Huntsville, Alabama. 2025 purchases of property and equipment were $3,862 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $13.4 million at December 31, 2025 (14% within 12 months); cloud revenue CAGR 24 percent 2018-2025

quarterly_data.signal: D-Wave 10-K, government sales: in addition to its partnership with Carahsoft (a government IT solutions provider) and 'awardable' status on the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office's Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace, D-Wave made an Advantage2 system operational at Davidson Technologies in Huntsville, Alabama and formed a new business unit dedicated to U.S. government adoption of its quantum computing products and services. D-Wave and Davidson Technologies worked with Anduril Industries on an initial proof-of-concept for missile-defense planning, in which D-Wave says its Stride hybrid solver delivered at least 10x faster time-to-solution than classical solvers (a proof of concept, not a deployment).
